Xeroderma pigmentosum involves a defect in nucleotide excision repair, which primarily targets bulky DNA lesions caused by ultraviolet (UV) light.  
UV light induces covalent bonds between adjacent thymine bases on the same DNA strand, forming thymine dimers.  
Without functional nucleotide excision repair, thymine dimers accumulate, leading to mutations and skin cancers.  
Deamination of cytosine, depurination, and single-strand breaks are not primarily linked to XP or UV damage repair defects.
